blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew (Ruralz Control upgrades)
blocking.issue: Step 4 describes rollback after finalize as `ruralz control restore`, with only one Node consequence: Nodes enrolled since the backup re-enroll. That understates what restore does according to Control plane and GitOps, which owns `ruralz control restore`. Restore runs only into an empty deployment. It needs a root-signed anchor set with a new online key, which opens a higher `storeEpoch`. It invalidates all sessions and API tokens. Unless the operator supplies a revocation list, it admits no Node certificate issued before the restore, so every Node, not just recently enrolled ones, serves detached until it re-enrolls. Operators who follow this document would plan a rollback that behaves differently from what the owning document specifies.
blocking.evidence: Line 165: "After it, rollback means `ruralz control restore` from the first backup, losing every later Control Store write (Rollouts, audit entries, Enrollments); Nodes enrolled since re-enroll." Control plane and GitOps, Backup, restore and `postgres`: "`ruralz control restore` runs only from the host CLI into an empty deployment. Before any delivery it needs a root-signed anchor set with a new online key, opening a higher `storeEpoch` ... It invalidates sessions and API tokens and re-applies an operator-supplied revocation list; without one, no Node certificate issued before the restore is admitted ... until its Node re-enrolls or the list arrives. Those Nodes serve detached."
blocking.fix: Rewrite the second half of step 4 as follows: "After it, rollback means `ruralz control restore` of the pre-upgrade backup into an empty N-1 deployment, which loses every later Control Store write (Rollouts, audit entries, Enrollments, revocations). Restore follows [Control plane and GitOps](../architecture/04-control-plane-and-gitops.md#backup-restore-and-postgres): a root-signed anchor set opens a new `storeEpoch`, sessions and API tokens are invalidated, and Nodes serve detached until an operator-supplied revocation list arrives or they re-enroll; Nodes enrolled after the backup always re-enroll." Also add one line to Figure 2's caption or the Upgrade order prose saying that the backup taken in step a is the one this restore uses.
